text:
Vegas arrives in Buffalo having won three of its last five, most recently 2-1 at Detroit, where the Golden Knights trailed in the third period and Trevor Connelly scored the winner with 1:42 left. They're without Parker Wotherspoon. Buffalo is 4-1-0 in its last five after a 5-2 win over Columbus, and it's missing Konsta Helenius, Justin Danforth and Matt Grzelcyk. The sharpest storyline is Jack Eichel, Victor Olofsson and Brayden McNabb all returning to the building where their careers began, with Eichel's 2021 trade to Vegas hitting its five-year anniversary.

The teams are close on chance quality. Vegas has taken 53% of the expected goals (the quality of shots each side gets) at five on five, Buffalo 50%, and our model has it 3.16 to 3.00 for Vegas. The gap that stands out is the penalty kill: Buffalo allows 0.78 expected goals a game shorthanded against Vegas's 0.48, and the Sabres take 4.1 penalties a game. In net, projected starters Adin Hill (-1.1 goals saved above expected, which measures saves beyond what the shots deserved) and Colten Ellis (+2.3) both have small samples. Ellis starts over Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen, who has 11 of Buffalo's 16 starts.

For Vegas, we like Eichel, with a 76% chance at a point and 31% to score. Olofsson, drafted 181st overall by Buffalo in 2014, is on a five-game point streak. For Buffalo, Tage Thompson has the best goal chance on either side at 38% and is one assist from 200 career. Rasmus Dahlin plays his 600th game, though that milestone isn't in our numbers.
